data.source_text_main_point: Protesters staged a symbolic act by having MPAA president Jack Valenti sign Betamax tapes, highlighting the irony that he previously condemned the VCR as a 'Boston strangler' despite the technology's legal protection, drawing a parallel to the current Supreme Court case over digital file-sharing.

statements.key_statement: A professional singer and coalition spokesperson argues that modern digital file-sharing differs fundamentally from older analog technology by allowing perfect copies, suggesting the original intent of the US Constitution's copyright clause was to promote progress rather than secure exclusive rights
statements.long_statement: A professional singer and spokesperson for the Recording Artists' Coalition notes that although Betamax technology created noticeably worse second copies, current digital file-sharing enables the spread of millions of exact reproductions. This person argues that the original text of the US Constitution's copyright clause was designed to advance the progress of useful arts, not to guarantee exclusive rights forever.
